name: Copperveil Switchback Crowd-Runner Set
description: A reversible mid-length jacket anchors this set — one side a muted copper-brown twill with faint diagonal texture, the other a washed slate-grey microweave that reads as generic transit worker at a glance. The jacket features a split-back panel with magnetic detach seams at the shoulder blades, accommodating tail geneware or spinal rig hardware without bunching. Concealed inside-chest channels run parallel to the sternum for flat holster inserts or folded tools, and a hidden inner hem pocket spans the full width of the back panel. Beneath it, a dense rust-amber henley in scanner-resistant polymerized cotton sits close to the body, collar high enough to obscure a neck-line neural port. The trousers are straight-leg in dark ochre canvas with reinforced kneepad pockets (empty by default, functional when loaded) and two thigh channels for quick-draw tool access. Footwear is a low-profile boot in oil-tanned synthetic leather, cork-composite sole for reduced acoustic signature on hard floors, ankle-height with a side-zip hidden under a fold of material. The whole look reads as a mid-Circuit shift worker running an errand — until the jacket flips.
functionality: Reversible jacket for rapid identity shift; split-back panel with magnetic detach seams for spinal rigs and tail geneware; dual sternum holster channels; full-width hidden hem pocket; thigh-channel trousers for tool access; reinforced knee pockets; low acoustic-signature footwear; scanner-resistant base layer
what_it_says: This person moves through crowds without snagging attention. The copper tones say working-class practicality, not poverty. The jacket flip says they've done this before. Runners who wear this are methodical, patient, and prefer to be three blocks gone before anyone knows a job happened.
worn_by: mid-tier fixers working below their usual grade
manufacturer: Driftmark Collective — unlicensed street label, Circuit District, M88
story_hooks: A runner flips the jacket mid-pursuit and walks past the pursuing security team — but the copper side has a distinctive repair patch their contact will recognize, blowing the switch.

The scanner-resistant henley is flagging at a checkpoint because someone swapped the genuine article with a knockoff — now the runner needs to bluff through a hand-scan with a concealed weapon in the sternum channel.
A fixer spots the Driftmark Collective label inside the jacket collar and immediately knows the runner's tier — raising or lowering their offered rate accordingly.

physical_description.visual_profile: A deceptively utilitarian layered silhouette that reads as anonymous transit-worker at first glance. The reversible jacket creates a shape-shifting aesthetic—copper-brown twill suggests wear and weathering, while the slate-grey reverse offers plausible deniability. Mid-length cut hits at hip, providing coverage without bulk. The split-back panel and magnetic shoulder seams hint at hardware accommodation without advertising it. Overall impression: someone who blends into Circuit District crowds but carries capacity.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed but not baggy—designed for movement and gear integration without excessive fabric. Jacket sits straight through shoulders with intentional ease at the back for spine-mounted augmentation. Henley compresses slightly against the torso, disappearing under layers. Trousers are straight-leg with functional room at thighs, tapering subtly at ankle. Boots fit snug around the foot, minimal silhouette.
physical_description.primary_material: Reversible jacket: muted copper-brown twill (one side) and washed slate-grey microweave (reverse). Henley: scanner-resistant polymerized cotton, rust-amber tone. Trousers: dark ochre canvas, heavy-weight. Boots: oil-tanned synthetic leather with cork-composite sole.
physical_description.texture: Twill side reads slightly napped and faded, diagonal weave visible under raking light. Microweave reverse is smooth and uniform, faintly ribbed, clinical. Henley fabric is dense and matte, slightly fuzzy from polymerization process. Canvas trousers have visible weave texture, worn soft at stress points. Boots show hand-finished aging on leather, subtle scuff marks from manufacturing.
physical_description.color_scheme: Copper-brown twill (warm, earthy, aged), slate-grey microweave (neutral, industrial), rust-amber henley (warm undertone, sits between the two jacket sides), dark ochre canvas (muted earth tone). No bright accents—all colors desaturated and functional. Monochromatic earth-tone palette with gray as the 'invisible' option.
physical_description.closures: Jacket: magnetic detach seams at shoulder blades for hardware pass-through; full front zip with friction-fit slider (unmarked). Henley: pull-over, no closures. Trousers: standard waistband with internal friction-fit closure, no visible hardware. Boots: side-zip hidden under folded leather flap, matte finish, minimal reflection.
distinctive_features: Split-back magnetic detach panels at shoulder blades for spinal rig or tail geneware accommodation
Concealed sternum-parallel channels for flat holster inserts or tool storage
Hidden full-width back-panel inner hem pocket
Reinforced kneepads with recessed pockets (functional when loaded, unobtrusive when empty)
Thigh-mounted quick-draw tool channels integrated into seam construction
High collar henley designed to obscure cervical neural ports
Side-zip boot hidden under folded leather flap for acoustic stealth
Cork-composite sole for reduced acoustic signature
Reversible jacket allows identity shift from copper-brown to slate-grey in seconds
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 4 — working class with street smarts. Driftmark Collective is unlicensed, suggesting resistance to corpo oversight. Build quality and material selection indicate someone who invests in functional gear rather than display status. Price point sits between disposable fast-fashion and corpo-grade equipment.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearer signals Circuit District worker, transit employee, or independent operator. The reversible design implies discretion—capable of shifting appearance for different contexts. Integrated hardware accommodation suggests either geneware heritage or cybernetic augmentation. Someone living in the margins of legality but not desperate: tool-focused, privacy-conscious, experienced with crowd navigation.
physical_description.condition_typical: Usually broken-in but functional. Magnetic seams show slight wear from repeated shoulder-movement attachment. Canvas knees develop subtle fading from kneeling. Boots show genuine scuff marks from urban wear. Henley collar shows minimal pilling at edges. The entire set has the patina of gear that's used, not displayed—but never neglected.
